terms.definition: The system used to build software with AI agents: sessions, subagents, workflows, scripts, gates and checks, memory, token management, the PC they run on, and how results reach the owner.
terms.origin: Coined by us (owner's usage) in docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md; not the FixFlow product.

terms.definition: The owner's earlier large clinic-management build on this PC, used to exercise and measure the harness. Its record is the source of the 21 bottlenecks and most measured numbers.
terms.origin: The owner's project; evidence summarised in docs/program/evidence/harness-bottlenecks/.

terms.definition: The workshop management product (home-appliance repair shop, Karachi) that the ship program delivers. It is the repository this harness work lives in, and one of two measured projects.
The owner's GIKI senior design project: rare-disease drug repurposing using routed specialist models, Neo4j and a checked language model. Harness research was mapped onto it.
The model that runs the main session as orchestrator, architect and judge. It does not run as a subagent.
terms.origin: Anthropic model (claude-fable-5-1); role set in docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md.

terms.definition: Strongest Anthropic tier in routine use here: deep subsystem analysis, architects, refuters, skeptics, critics and fresh-context verification. Opus 5.5 compacts by itself near 367k tokens.
Mid-tier Anthropic model used for discovery, mapping, web collection, scouts, citation checks, gates and blind readers; the cheap model in the library plan.
Smallest, cheapest Anthropic tier here, used only for typed extraction and locating where code lives (the fixflow-explorer agent).
Relative list price of new tokens for Fable:Opus:Sonnet:Haiku, used to convert model calls into cheap-call equivalents in the library model.
terms.origin: Outside price list checked 2026-11-12; recorded in memory/project-library-plausibility-review.md.

terms.definition: Codex is another vendor's coding agent, tested as an adapter target and proposed as an outside second reviewer (not taken now). gpt-6-astra is the model name recorded in the Codex evaluation runs.
The testbed's snapshot-and-restore tool around compaction, built for Codex and evaluated three times.
terms.origin: Clinic testbed, built for OpenAI Codex.

terms.definition: A per-agent setting for how much reasoning a model spends. Raised before moving up a model tier; xhigh is highest and costs most.
terms.origin: Claude Code and Anthropic model setting.

terms.definition: The long-lived top session that plans, briefs, reads results and diffs, judges gates, merges and edits shared files. Its window is the largest token cost measured.
terms.origin: Claude Code session role; named in docs/ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN-2026-10.md and the clinic orchestration.

terms.definition: In the ship plan's parallel execution, the single session on the plan branch that owns the plan, shared results, contracts and the merge call, and never writes feature code.
terms.origin: Coined by us in SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md section 7.1.

terms.definition: One Claude Code session working one slice or phase in its own git worktree in parallel with others, ending in a draft PR.
terms.origin: Coined in the harness v2 design and ship plan section 7.1.

terms.term: Lane names (B-core, B-jobs, B-att, B-tools, M, W, O, L, OWN)
terms.definition: Ship-plan work areas: B-core backend core, B-jobs jobs and money, B-att attendance, B-tools scripts, M mobile, W web, O ops, L lab, OWN the owner's own steps.
terms.origin: Coined by us in SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md section 7.3.

terms.definition: One bounded unit of build work with its own branch, worktree and record, that is checked, reviewed and merged. Slice sessions used 66.4 % of November tokens.
A group of slices or lanes run in parallel once their dependencies merge; ship plan waves A-D set the lane start order.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic build and SHIP-PLAN section 7.6.

terms.definition: A separate Claude agent started by a session or workflow to do one task and return a result. Each pays a fixed prefix cost before working.
The multi-agent mode whose token cost multiplies across agents, so the model and effort per agent matter.
Investigation stage names: W0 owner pre-flight with no agents, W1 wide cheap discovery (16 agents), W2 narrow expensive deep dive (8 analysts), S3 the later phase plan.
Written records by the main session after W1 (G1) and W2 (G2) giving hypothesis verdicts, the verified defect register and decisions, before the next workflow is dispatched.
A check or review a change must pass before merging: tests, lint, claim checks and reviewers finding no open critical defect. Also the step that runs a store entry's own check.
terms.origin: General software practice; gate workflow coined in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 3.4.

terms.definition: A plain JavaScript workflow script that gathers agent results and derives buckets for the Fable judge.

terms.term: Task ID scheme (H-01, S-01a, R-01, O-01)
terms.definition: H = Haiku extractor, S = Sonnet mapper or gate runner, R = research agent, O = Opus analyst; numbers are stable labels used for resume.
A saved JavaScript script run by the Workflow tool that issues subagents in a defined order via agent(prompt, {schema, model, effort}) and returns one structured result.
A per-run log of completed agent results that lets a stopped workflow resume from its run id; knownDead lists ids that returned null last time.
terms.origin: Claude Code workflow feature; knownDead use coined by us.

terms.definition: A script rule that stops issuing agents when fresh null results suggest a usage limit, halting with HALT and not_started lists.
terms.origin: Software engineering pattern; applied in ORCHESTRATION-DESIGN section 4.3.

terms.definition: A fixed text prepended to every subagent prompt giving repo, branch, settled facts and rules.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the orchestration design and clinic launcher.

terms.definition: Project instruction files every agent session reads first. FixFlow's is about 7.5k tokens and 390 lines; AGENTS.md is the equivalent convention for other agent tools.
A typed shape for agent output; additionalProperties:false forbids extra fields. A description keyword attaches plain-language meaning to a property.
The forced tool call a schema-bearing subagent must make to return its answer; validated by the tool layer and retried on mismatch.
Stage-1 agents return facts only, never comparisons, severities or verdicts; judgement is left to the main session.
The Opus agent that reads the live repository in a deep-dive lane and returns ranked, evidenced findings. Analysts produce claims; skeptics check them.
A fresh-context Opus verifier given only a claim, its evidence and failing condition, asked to trace or refute it; capped at 12 at G2.
A fresh-context agent (usually Opus, xhigh) whose job is to disprove a claim, fix or design; default verdict is refuted, so an idea must survive counter-evidence.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the orchestration method and harness sweeps.

terms.definition: A review stance and reviewer role: assume the claim or change is wrong until code and tests show otherwise.
terms.origin: Coined in the clinic build, ship plan section 0 and agent definitions.

terms.definition: A Sonnet pass confirming quoted text exists where claimed and has not moved or been fixed.
Skeptic outcomes; unverifiable means neither proven nor disproven and carries a settling test.
A review result in a fixed machine-readable form that names the head commit read.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the bottleneck compile.

terms.definition: The input or state under which a defect claim is observable.
Claims not verified or refuted, kept with the test that would settle them.
Finding severity from most to least serious. P1 late fixes created new defects; 183 P3 ids were carried unstatused in the testbed.
terms.origin: Common triage convention; scheme used in G2 and the clinic reviews.

terms.definition: Check only items touched by a change, plus files one import away.
A markdown file naming a helper agent with its own prompt, tools and pinned model; selected through agentType or subagent_type. We have 11 fixflow-* agents.
Two project agents: a Haiku code locator, and a PR reviewer bound to a head commit that returns a verdict schema.
terms.origin: Built by us in this repository.

terms.definition: Claude Code's built-in file-finding agent; it inherits the session model's tier.
A folder of instructions an agent loads for a kind of task, starting with a SKILL.md whose description says when to use it. We have 13 skill packages.
The header block of an agent file; its skills field loads the named skill's full text at agent start.
UPSTREAM.md is provenance for a sourced skill package (repo, commit, paths, licence, date). SPDX is the standard short licence identifier, e.g. MIT.
terms.origin: UPSTREAM.md coined in .claude/skills/README.md; SPDX is an outside standard.

terms.definition: A step only the human owner may perform; agents stop there.

terms.term: Output shapes (MAP, RESEARCH, FINDINGS, VERDICT, COMMANDS, SCAN)
terms.definition: Fixed schemas agents return; FINDINGS is an analyst's ranked claims, VERDICT a skeptic's ruling, SCAN reports committed secrets as fingerprints.
Claude Code tools; web tools must be loaded through ToolSearch before use.
A session-specific temporary folder outside the repository where agents write logs and working files.

terms.term: Hook (PreCompact, SessionStart, PostCompact, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop)
terms.definition: A script Claude Code runs automatically at an event, such as before compaction, at session start, or on stop; it can add text, block, or alter a tool call.
A PostToolUse hook route that replaces a tool's result before the model sees it.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature (per the runtime audit).

terms.definition: A project settings block in .claude/settings.json listing commands the agent may not run.
Claude Code permission mode in which subagents run without asking approval.
SendMessage messages a running session. A parked start is a session created now and released later by message.
terms.origin: SendMessage: Claude Code tool; parked start coined by us (card CR-02).

terms.definition: get_usage reports a session's tokens used and compactions; /context shows what fills the window (skills, MCP, CLAUDE.md).
terms.origin: Claude Code desktop and CLI features.

terms.definition: Claude Code's non-interactive command-line mode, one process per prompt.
The saved record of a Claude Code session, one JSON line per message or call; pruned after 30 days by default. JSONL is the one-record-per-line format.
terms.origin: Claude Code feature; JSON Lines general format.

terms.definition: Model Context Protocol, the standard for plugging tools and data sources into Claude; a connector is a linked outside service whose tool definitions add to window size.
The unit of text a model reads or writes; usage, cost and window size are counted in tokens.
Everything the model sees on one call: system prompt, tools, earlier messages and results. A ceiling near 367k applies in practice.
Tokens the model read, summed over every call, including cache reads.
Tokens re-read from the prompt cache on each call at a lower price; summed over calls they measure how much context is carried (4,253M in November).
Tokens newly stored in the cache, counted separately from cache reads.
A feature storing a repeated prompt start so later calls read it cheaply.
Tokens the model writes, including thinking; 45 % of them were thinking in the token study.
One request to the model, which re-reads the whole window; the message id is its unique id, used to count each call once.

terms.term: Fixed prefix / fixed cost per agent
terms.definition: The roughly 70,000 tokens (system prompt, tool and connector schemas, skills, CLAUDE.md) each agent re-reads before doing work; tool definitions are 34k of it.
terms.origin: Claude Code subagent behaviour; measurement card CR-11.

terms.term: Tool and connector schemas / deferred tool schemas
terms.definition: Descriptions of every tool and connector loaded into the window. Deferred schemas list tools by name only and load full text when needed, shrinking the prefix.
Claude Code replacing a long conversation with a summary (plus a verbatim tail) so the session can continue; 48 occurred in main sessions in November.
Claude Code setting (100000-1000000) naming the token size that triggers automatic compaction; a 400000 setting compacts near 367k.
A compaction using a summary precomputed while the session was idle (default on, threshold 200k tokens).
The summary left after compaction, re-read on every later call (8 % of context tokens in the study).
The plan's cap on use within a rolling five-hour period; when reached all work stops. How cache reads count against it is unknown.
The harness's own spend counter; its totals are a lower bound (about one-third coverage).
A change that could cut token use, ranked by size in the token report.
How much of the tokens sit where an idea or lever could act (for example calls past 200k); it is neither a saving nor a ceiling.
terms.origin: Coined in the bottleneck compile and token report.

terms.definition: The small group of files holding half the fetched tokens across sessions.
A short repo file of state, decisions, ruled-out items and next action that a session reads to resume; the clinic task.md also held the status table and gate sections.
terms.origin: Convention in the FixFlow and clinic harnesses.

terms.definition: Only the root edits shared documents.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic orchestration page.

terms.definition: The written instruction given to a session or subagent.
Fan-out is children per parent; depth is levels of sessions below the root (here root, slice sessions, at most one child level).
Labels REPORTED, OBSERVED, DOCUMENTED, INFERRED, PROPOSED, UNKNOWN and VERIFIED stating how a fact is known.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic AGENTS.md.

terms.definition: Ids of the 21 unsolved bottlenecks of the testbed build, listed by the clinic root on 2026-11-11 (e.g. B01 fix rounds, B04 serial orchestrator, B12 reports overstate, B17 unread final heads). Distinct from loop ids B1-B5.
Ids of mechanism cards extracted from testbed records: A is the sweep (A5 context system, A6 corpus map), CR the root's compaction and context lessons. 158 cards.
Bottleneck classes: Build means remedy known; Decide is the owner's choice; Diagnose means a measurement finds the cause; Trial is plausible but unmeasured.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the 2026-11-11 compile.

terms.term: Number tags M, E, G, S, T, I
terms.definition: Evidence tags on every number: M measured, E estimated, G guess, S a setting or outside study or price list, T target, I illustrative. A computed number takes the weakest input tag.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the harness documents.

terms.definition: Direct: the idea would move the number in a bottleneck's Proof column. Supporting: it makes a step of the first move cheaper, safer or checkable.
terms.origin: Coined in the bottleneck compile section 9.2.

terms.definition: The eleven artefacts the 29 fitting ideas reduce to: replay seal, verdict script, transcript audit, finding table, stub harness, merge queue, command-backed facts, resume guard, fix-round clauses, owner read, tool allow-list.
terms.origin: Coined in the bottleneck compile section 9.3.

terms.definition: Prefer deterministic scripts over prompts or model re-checks for guarding quality, because prose rules and re-checks failed here.
terms.origin: Coined in the bottleneck compile section 7.

terms.definition: The earlier map of 21 bottlenecks and idea fit, docs/program/HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS-2026-11.md.
Mapper: an agent placing each idea against the bottlenecks. Adjudicator: an agent ruling on flagged items; default stays dropped.
terms.origin: Roles in the compile's section 9 workflows.

terms.definition: Outside practitioner, founder of HumanLayer and author of 12-Factor Agents and the research-plan-implement method, whose published work (since 2025-06-01) was swept for harness ideas (PR #186).
Dex Horthy's company, behind the repositories, docs and talks that fed the sweep; it joined Factory on 2026-11-04.
A second author whose material contributed 97 of the 1,906 Horthy-sweep cards.
A weekly show hosted by Vaibhav Gupta (BAML) and Dex Horthy; 582 of the 1,906 cards come from its episodes.

Tessl: a podcast episode read in the addendum. AGNTCon talk (2026-10-22): 'There Is No Software Factory Without Better Verifiers', with no recording, so not inferred. <important if>: Horthy's March 2026 tagging of conditional rules.

Outside benchmark of how maintainable agent-written code stays over successive features; Horthy's October 2026 report found medium effort often matched or beat xhigh at lower cost. Strict pass is its strictest score.
terms.origin: Outside study (Gabe Orlanski, reported by Dex Horthy).

terms.definition: Horthy's name for the stretch of a long context window where quality degrades; set at 100k tokens in mid-2025, later withdrawn as a flat figure.
Scripts and checks that push back on an agent with short failure output, so errors are fed back cheaply and noise is kept out of context.
A wrapper writing full test logs to a file and printing one line; our Appendix A g() does this for backend gates.
terms.origin: HumanLayer hack/run_silent.sh; ours coined in Appendix A.

terms.definition: Horthy's three-stage method: research the code, write a plan, then implement.
Running an agent in a repeating loop on a task.
terms.origin: Geoff Huntley; popularised by Dex Horthy.

terms.definition: Prompt-injection risk when an agent has untrusted content, private data and external communication at once.
terms.origin: Simon Willison, cited in HumanLayer material.

terms.definition: The idea of automated code-production loops; Horthy argues there is none without better verifiers.
fxtwitter is a public API returning X posts without login; faster-whisper distil-large-v3 is a local speech-to-text model used to transcribe recordings on the GPU.

terms.term: Horthy-sweep terms: card, family, blind reader, Reviewers A and B
terms.definition: Card: one extracted idea with quote and claim (1,906). Family: cluster of cards with the same claim (838, then 861). Blind reader: Sonnet that read without knowing our harness. Reviewers A (benefit-seeker) and B (cost-and-novelty skeptic) scored each family.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the Horthy sweep (PR #186).

terms.definition: The ruling on an idea family: adopt as is, trial with a measured test first, already done by the harness, or skip for weak evidence or low value.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the Horthy and BAML sweeps.

terms.definition: Narrowed: the refuter let only a smaller version of the idea survive, and that form is what tables list. Over the cap: a family that reached no refuter because the per-group limit was hit.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the Horthy sweep.

terms.definition: A second pass adding 36 sources and 311 cards (X posts, SlopCodeBench article, Tessl episode, local transcriptions) without re-clustering.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the Horthy document section 4.

terms.definition: Ids of Horthy idea families: group number then family number, e.g. G2-F118. G1-G4 are idea groups.
terms.origin: Coined in the Horthy sweep, PR #186.

terms.definition: The five weaknesses ideas were scored against: W1 CLAUDE.md length, W2 self-reported compliance, W3 routine never run (cold resume), W4 few agents and skills, W5 workflows not saved. Not the same as the W0-W2 stages.
Three levers ideas were scored against: L1 effort routing, L2 context budget and compaction, L3 output backpressure and verifiers. Not the ship-plan L1-L4 phases.
A language for typed LLM functions that parse model replies into typed objects. Assessed for generic ideas, not adopted as a tool (PR #184); v0 is legacy DSL, v1 pre-1.0.
The company that makes BAML; its podcast, post-mortems and benchmarks were quoted in the sweep.
BAML's method of putting the schema in the prompt and repairing the reply to fit; the harness instead rejects a bad reply.

terms.term: BAML item ids (B-, D-, I-, P-, R-, S-, T-)
terms.definition: Ids of the 89 BAML idea cards by source lane: B blog, D docs, I independent evidence, P prior art, R repo, T talks; S-1..S-5 are structural borrows. Dispositions e.g. D-13 definitions, S-3 stub run, T-08 record-only checks.
terms.origin: Coined in the BAML sweep, PR #184.

terms.definition: The BAML assessment's five 0-3 scores: evidence quality, transferability, novelty, expected benefit, and cost and risk (3 is cheap and safe).
Two ways BAML could run here: A uses claude -p with Claude Code tools on the subscription; B uses API-keyed typed functions with hand-written tools.
terms.origin: Coined in the BAML structural comparison.

terms.definition: A canary-only BAML v1 client running one claude -p process per turn. Canary and nightly are BAML's pre-release channels; v1 has no stable release.
BAML rules: @assert rejects a bad value, @check records a named pass or fail and keeps the value. Collector records every attempt per call.
A billed Anthropic reply (HTTP 200, stop_reason refusal) returned when a schema asks for the model's reasoning.

terms.term: Pydantic AI / Instructor / TypeChat / DSPy / GEPA
terms.definition: Outside frameworks cited as prior art: offline test models, schema validation with bounded repair, and prompt optimisation (GEPA, Genetic Pareto, from the DSPy authors).
BFCL: Berkeley function-calling leaderboard. Constrained decoding forces tokens to a grammar and needs logit access. Schema-echo: reply repeats the schema. TOON: compact input text format.
terms.origin: UC Berkeley benchmark; general LLM field; BAML evaluations.

terms.definition: A fake stand-in for agent() returning canned objects (nothing, throw, refute) so a script's bookkeeping is tested with no model, at zero tokens.
terms.origin: General testing; BAML sweep item S-3 (PR #184); Pydantic AI TestModel is prior art.

terms.definition: An allowed value such as UNVERIFIABLE or unknown that lets an agent say the input does not fit instead of inventing an answer.
The pull request on the plan branch docs/orchestration-design-2026-10 holding the ship plan, design notes and evidence; not merged to main.
The pull request holding the knowledge-store design.
The pull requests holding the BAML sweep (#184) and the Horthy sweep (#186) with their verdicts on each idea.
The draft pull request holding the 13 skill packages and 11 fixflow agents.
FixFlow's sequenced plan to get shipped, on PR #182. Versions: v6 from the harness review, v7 and v8 after delta checks, v9 added parallel execution, v9.3 delegated merging to the coordinator.

terms.term: Phase ids (P0a, P1, P2a, P7a, P13e ... and L1-L4)
terms.definition: Named phases of the ship plan, each meant to fit one session. P is a product phase, L a harness-infrastructure phase (L1 gate harness, L3 device lab), a letter suffix a sub-part.
The owner's pre-flight: hold notice, Railway state, R2 archive, Supabase dump, phone roster and builds. The harness work must not delay it.
First line of a phase PR body naming the exact commit of the ship plan in force; a resume re-reads the plan diff from it.
terms.origin: Adopted from Horthy-style practice; ship plan HR-C2.

terms.definition: The owner's one-line-per-phase status page updated at phase close.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the ship plan.

terms.definition: A test where a fresh agent must recover ten frozen facts from the repository and PR alone, proving a phase can resume.
terms.origin: Coined in the ship plan (P1 trial).

terms.definition: The planned adherence experiment: 10 direct probes with a frozen rubric testing whether agents obey CLAUDE.md under different layouts or models.
HARNESS-REVIEW-2026-11-01.md and its labelled rulings (HR-A1a, HR-C1, HR-C4 ...), binding on the plan from v6; HR-C4 is the 500k context trigger needing a sensor.
One of four Opus agents each reviewing the architecture from one viewpoint, such as offline sync or Android platform.
A critic pass that reads only what changed between plan versions.
The table of verified findings with ids, severity and status (103 rows). A register id names a known defect a reviewer must check is fixed, with a fail-before and pass-after test.
terms.origin: Coined at G2 and in the ship plan.

terms.definition: Analyst number plus finding number; O01-F20 is analyst O-01's finding 20.
Register statuses: V skeptic-confirmed, S skeptic-narrowed, C corroborated, G gap or design, O open.
Citation-check outcomes DEAD_CITATION, ALREADY_FIXED and MOVED (line drift).
Numbered possible causes of the field system's failures, with verdicts at G1. FixFlow product questions, not harness ideas.
docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-open-work.md, the earlier document of open work and the list of known defects used as a baseline.
Named failure shapes from the clinic record about verification that goes green without testing anything, e.g. RT-01 a check must be able to fail, RT-06 unknown is not zero.
terms.origin: Clinic tasks folder; harness review section 4.

terms.definition: M00-M06 is the clinic's skipped measurement pipeline of recurring evals; WF-01..WF-04 are its workflow research stages (pilot, trial, measurement research, expansion).
A fix is evidenced by a test that fails (by assertion) on the base commit and passes on the head commit.
terms.origin: General testing practice; stricter rule from G4-F086.

terms.definition: Git commit id at the tip of a branch (head) or where it branched (base). A reviewer verdict is bound to the head SHA it read.
A separate checked-out working copy of a git repository on its own branch, one per slice or lane session (19 existed on this PC).
Squash merge lands a PR as one commit; cherry-pick copies a commit onto another branch; patch-id hashes a change so it matches after squashing.
A single file holding a repository's history, usable as an off-machine backup.

terms.term: Build-ahead / entry line / stack / at risk / merge-hold list
terms.definition: Starting a phase before its entry condition is met when the unmet item is not code it needs; stacking on a reviewed branch tip; labelling the PR at risk; and keeping a list of PRs held as draft.
terms.origin: Coined by us in SHIP-PLAN-2026-11.md section 7.2.

terms.definition: The review the coordinator dispatches by a fresh Opus agent on the PR head SHA; a PR is merge-ready when gates and CI are green, the verdict names the head SHA, it is not held and the coordinator read it.
Git tags on plan commits so a lane reads exactly the commit it cites.
The plan's section 0 rules, the owner's rulings and human-review amendments that the parallel-execution section leaves unchanged.
terms.origin: Coined in the v8 ship plan and harness review.

terms.definition: ff-gates.sh runs backend, mobile or web checks in containers with a per-lane database; ff-slot.sh is the machine-wide lock. A slot is one heavy-job permit (3, or 2 during Gradle).
A machine-wide permit for running the full test check; others wait. The clinic had two slots, with waits up to 2,030 s.
terms.origin: Coined in the testbed faster-check task.

terms.definition: The clinic's full application check: ruff, format, mypy, Django checks, migrations, database probe, pytest. Container mode runs it inside a Linux Docker container (230 s versus 367 s on Windows).
pytest-xdist runs tests in parallel workers; the serial pass is a second run for tests that cannot run in parallel, such as race tests.
terms.origin: Open-source pytest plugin; serial pass coined by us.

terms.definition: The lane or worker count where the lowest limit is reached; beyond it extra lanes add queues and tokens but no speed (between 6 and 12 workers in the testbed).
A periodic signal naming what a long check is doing, and a timer that kills a silent check; the stall limit is 600 s. The check writes waiting, running or stalled.
A Windows feature that kills a whole process tree when its owner dies.
A script that merges slices one at a time under a lock, runs the check on the merged result and applies the board diff.
terms.origin: Coined in the bottleneck compile section 3.4 and designed in harness v2.

terms.definition: Planner picks lane count before work; scheduler starts and resumes sessions; governor throttles lanes to fit the token window.
terms.origin: Coined in the harness v2 design.

terms.definition: The list of files a slice declares it will write; the plan check uses it to avoid collisions.
terms.origin: Coined in harness v2 plan check.

terms.definition: Reinforcing (R) and balancing (B) feedback loops: R1 fix spiral, R2 context growth, R3 library compounds, R4 pile-up, B1 check capacity, B2 serial gate, B3 limit stop, B4 staleness, B5 lanes at knee.
terms.origin: System dynamics; named in harness v2 design.

terms.definition: Model quantities (stocks, such as slices waiting) and the rates moving them between states (flows).
Owner decision cards on the harness v2 page, each with a phase and when it is needed.
terms.origin: Coined in the harness v2 design.

terms.definition: Re-running a recorded fix chain or review at a frozen commit in a clone with no later refs and a hashed answer key, so the agent cannot see the fix.
terms.origin: Coined in the compile sections 4 and 9.3 (from G2-F051).

terms.definition: A script mode that writes down what it would refuse or flag but blocks nothing, so it can be validated before it gets power.
The record listing every review finding with severity and status; testbed rows were prose thousands of characters long, so a table is proposed.
A list of permitted forms (citation styles, tools) so legitimate items are not flagged or refused.
A cleanup script removing finished sessions or worktrees; dry run first, so it only reports what it would remove.
terms.origin: Coined in the compile for B15.

terms.definition: A first-use walk on an empty database with no synthetic data, through first user, import, transaction and close of day.
A case that must be detected, proving the check can find something; every nothing-found check needs one.
Deliberate adversarial testing of a mechanism; eight red-team defects were still open.
Removing one lock to prove the named test fails without it; a race test runs two concurrent actions to prove a lock stops a conflict.
terms.origin: Coined in the clinic gate; general testing.

terms.definition: Numbered owner decisions on the clinic board: 21 root may start next slices itself; 22 approve parallel-test dependency; 23 use the machine and a Linux container; 24 wrap up the build.
terms.origin: Owner decision log of the clinic build.

terms.definition: Numbered clinic review findings; letters name the slice or review family (GS, GT, GU, GV; faster-check FC and FS).
terms.origin: Coined in the clinic task.md board.

terms.definition: Findings moved out of the gates to be fixed during the pilot; T15, T16, T17 are plan acceptance targets (T17 page latency and load).
terms.origin: Owner decision USER-24; clinic technical plan.

terms.definition: A script creating fake test data; real labels without the SYN marker are refused by design.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the clinic build.

terms.definition: A local Debian virtual machine sized like the proposed server, running fifteen re-runnable drills (deploy, upgrade, backup, restore, load, security probe).
Locust is an open-source load tester; N+1 is a page issuing many small database queries; fsync=off is a Postgres setting skipping disk flushes, safe only for disposable test databases.
terms.origin: Outside open-source projects and database practice.

terms.definition: Windows socket state and the 'No buffer space available' error seen on loopback connections.
Ceiling on speed-up when only part of the work can be removed: 1/(1-X).
Outside study finding AI access raised task completion time 19 percent (early-2025, 16 developers).
Open-source tools for evaluating and tracing language-model runs.
Outside agent-engineering projects audited by the clinic alongside HumanLayer.
A rule-of-thumb token estimate that undercounts by about 25-35 percent in this repository.
Agent-written memory notes loaded each session (15 files in the clinic root).

terms.term: Context system (snapshot/restore, read admission, recall, resident input)
terms.definition: The clinic's tool around compaction: snapshot saves declared task-state before compaction and restores it verbatim; read admission limits file reads (over 30 KB); recall searches transcripts by words; resident input is what sits in the window per request.
terms.origin: Coined by us in tools/context_system (card line A5).

terms.term: Corpus map (cmap), status model S1-S6, query levels L1-L3, frontier, dangling endpoint
terms.definition: A versioned map of the clinic's planning documents with edges and line spans, built by cmap.py. Statuses: attested, codebook, overlay, reconstructed, candidate, derived. A frontier is unexpanded referents; a dangling endpoint is a named but unspecified target.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the corpus-map design (card line A6).

terms.term: Reader / reducer / pre-registration / arm / gates G0-G5
terms.definition: Map-programme roles and method: reader extracts, reducer re-fetches and checks quotes; pre-registration fixes test, gates and budget in writing before running; an arm is one condition in a comparison; G0-G5 are research checkpoints the orchestrator re-runs.
terms.origin: Coined in the map programme run.md; general scientific method.

terms.term: MemTree / LCM / Virtual Context / YesMem / Cairn / Headroom / squeez / context-mode / claude-mem / CCH
terms.definition: Outside memory, compression and context-capping tools audited by the clinic survey; each bounds only part of what enters the window; none adopted.
Open-source Python tool that builds a knowledge graph from a mixed corpus using tree-sitter; its 71.5x claim compares tokens per graph query with reading every raw file. A comparator arm.

terms.term: Call graph / blast radius / touch list
terms.definition: A map of which functions call which; blast radius or touch list is the set of functions, callers, importers, co-changing files and tests a fix could affect, attached to a reviewer brief.
terms.origin: General software practice; script proposed in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 6.

terms.definition: tree-sitter is a local code parser for about 40 languages; ast-grep searches code by syntax tree using it.
Tools that fail the build when code crosses forbidden module boundaries: dependency-cruiser for JavaScript, import-linter for Python.
A hand-written map of where each capability lives in each runtime.
Prompting schemes that have the model write several partial answers, branch, vote or merge them; showed no gain on current models.
Outside benchmark of real GitHub issues for coding agents, used to test fix-selection methods (a vote alone resolved 25.7 %).
Spatial: a thing's neighbourhood in code and work. Temporal: when a fact was true and when it was replaced.
terms.origin: Coined by us in HARNESS-BOTTLENECKS section 6.

terms.definition: How often two files change in the same commit, used as a signal for which files belong together (recall 0.26 in the graph test).
A ranking scoring nodes by how many well-linked nodes point to them; the personalised version restarts from a seed file so scores favour its neighbourhood. Also used by Aider's repo-map.
Recall: share of true items found; precision: share of returned items true. recall@8k is the share of reference files and definitions inside an 8,000-token answer, the graph test's primary metric.
One link step in a graph; 3 hops reaches things three links from the seed.
Hub: a file many others depend on. Metapath: a typed route through the graph, such as calls, then client URL, then route, then handler, then table write.
A graph whose nodes and links each carry a kind and evidence (file and line); symbol-level means nodes are functions, classes and components rather than files.
A graph where a model reads text and code and writes meaning into it; a TKG also records when each fact became true and was superseded. Our parser-built graph was neither.
terms.origin: General AI field; outside systems such as Graphiti and Zep.

terms.term: Graphiti / Mem0 / Letta / Zep / Copilot Memory
terms.definition: Outside agent-memory products cited for ideas (two clocks, retire-don't-delete, just-in-time re-verification) and failure modes; Graphiti is a temporal knowledge-graph client also found elsewhere on this PC.

terms.term: GraphRAG / HippoRAG / RepoGraph / LocAgent / Aider repo-map
terms.definition: Outside systems using graphs to help models retrieve or localise code, cited as prior art with mixed results; Aider's repo-map is a tree-sitter outline ranked by personalised PageRank within a token budget.
terms.origin: Outside papers and the Aider tool.

terms.definition: LadybugDB 0.22.3 is an embedded graph database, the maintained fork of Kuzu, whose upstream was archived in 2025; one graph-engine arm.
DuckDB is an embedded analytical SQL database; DuckPGQ is its extension adding property-graph queries.
A widely used graph database server (JVM); candidate engine, not installed.
SQLite is a small file-based database; FTS5 is its built-in full-text search with BM25 ranking; a recursive query follows links over several steps.
The 1.26 GB Linux Docker image in which every graph-test arm runs.
The seed is the changed file or symbol given as the query; the reference is the other files and definitions that same commit changed.

terms.term: T1 / T1x / T2 / T3 / T4 / T5 / TQ
terms.definition: Graph-test task sets: T1 change completion; T1x its cross-runtime subset; T2 changed code to tests; T3 documented chains; T4 defect register; T5 document lookups; TQ code-reading questions.
Hypotheses declared in advance: H1/H2 engines equal; H1b community prior; H3 typed vs baselines; H4 questions; H5 engine speed and size.
The 65 June commits used to choose settings (tune) and the 75 July-August commits scored once for the verdict (held-out).
A cheap baseline (same directory, plain co-change, or scripted search) that any graph method must beat to count.
terms.origin: Coined in the graph test addendum 2.

terms.definition: The search baseline run as a script rather than an agent deciding what to search.
A stored grouping of related nodes (Louvain community detection) added to the ranking as a prior.
A 95 % interval from 10,000 resamples by commit, and a permutation test for paired differences between arms.
Rank-quality scores: mean reciprocal rank, normalised discounted gain at ten, and area under the recall-against-tokens curve.
Many random re-runs of a model with unknown settings drawn from their ranges, to get a spread and ranking rather than one answer.
A statistic showing how steadily one number rises or falls as another rises across runs; used to rank which unknowns move a result most.
Bounds on a rate from few trials: zero failures in n trials means the true rate is under about 3/n (0 in 40 gives 7.5 %); Clopper-Pearson gives the exact one-sided bound.

terms.term: P@1 / recall at shown / acted false positive
terms.definition: P@1 is precision of the top result; recall at shown is how many true entries appear in what is displayed; an acted false positive is a wrong lead someone acted on.
Calibration that removes one key from an entry and checks it is still found.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval evaluation; named in lane T-03.

terms.definition: Planned local database plus command-line tool where agents record solved hard problems, traps and failed approaches and later look them up by symptom. Designed in PR #183, not built.
The journal is an append-only folder of immutable event files in git (the truth); the index is a disposable SQLite database rebuilt from it for fast lookups.
terms.origin: Event-sourcing pattern; proposal D in the design.

terms.definition: Entry: one stored lesson. Handle: a key it is found by (error template, symbol, paraphrase). Footprint: files, settings and versions it depends on, used to notice staleness.
terms.origin: Coined by us; footprint adapted from build-system dependency tracking.

terms.definition: Lookup outcomes: lead is a confident, gate-checked match, candidate a weaker one, miss nothing. Abstention is answering nothing when unsure.
Retrieval thresholds 0.5, 0.3 and margin 0.2 deciding lead, candidate and miss; frozen at KS-4.

terms.term: Trace / early cutoff / control pair / inject-control
terms.definition: Trace: fingerprint of the footprint at the last passing check. Early cutoff: keep an entry if its check still passes after a dependency changed. Control pair: two commits where the check must read present then absent. Inject-control re-applies the failing pattern.
terms.origin: Build Systems a la Carte (ICFP 2018); controls coined by us.

terms.term: Probe / mutant / probe-in-lookup / valid_when / tri-state verdict
terms.definition: A probe is a small automatic check that a root cause is present; a mutant is a harmless edit it must ignore; probe-in-lookup runs it inside the lookup; valid_when is a precondition; verdicts are applies, not_applies, inconclusive.
terms.origin: Coined by us; mutation-testing idea from software testing.

terms.term: Entry kinds (do_not_apply, open_defect, trap, unverified_seed, pending_anchor)
terms.definition: A forbidden change, an unfixed defect, a gotcha, an entry awaiting its executable check, and an entry whose fix sits on a branch.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design.

terms.term: Write gate / diff lookup / false-fire ceiling / caller-pin test / second door
terms.definition: Write gate checks on recording; diff lookup (ks lookup --diff) warns when a PR touches protected code; false-fire ceiling is one commit in ten; a caller-pin test fixes allowed callers; a second door skips a guard.
terms.origin: Coined by us (KS-2, D8, D17; owner critique 2026-11-03).

terms.definition: The knowledge store's build phases, one session each: audit, journal core, retrieval, gate, seed, pilot, Docker gates, wire-in, second host, checkpoint; KS-6b is the executable gate; T is teardown.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design.

terms.definition: Rulings (R), adjudication (A), refuted claims (C), refuter amendments (F), critic amendments (K), owner-critique items (O1..O20), refuter-pass amendments (P1..P27), second-pass claims (V).
terms.origin: Coined by us in sections 12.1-12.8 of the knowledge-store design.

terms.definition: Numbered owner decisions each with a default, e.g. D1 run the free audit, D1b build go-ahead, D16 embedding trigger, D17 CI caller-pin test, D22 guarded_refs.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the knowledge-store design.

terms.definition: Eight real past defects reconstructed from git history as the first entries and test cases (ex6 correct-PIN account lock, ex3 payment duplicate, ex4 dispatcher cursor, ex7/ex8 Expo build traps).
terms.origin: Research lane R-02, coined by us.

terms.definition: BM25 is a word-matching ranking formula whose scores only order results within a query; IDF weights rare words; IDF-weighted coverage is the share of query rare-word weight an entry matches.
terms.origin: Information-retrieval field; built into SQLite FTS5.

terms.definition: Node's built-in SQLite module (release candidate) and settings letting many readers and one writer share a file safely and wait briefly when busy.

terms.term: Stampede / single-flight / claim / fencing token / Lamport counter
terms.definition: Several sessions repeating costly work; a claim lets the first proceed; a fencing token (claim_seq) marks a stale holder; a Lamport counter orders events from several writers.
terms.origin: Caching practice; Martin Kleppmann; Leslie Lamport.

terms.definition: A file named by the sha256 of its own sorted-key JSON bytes, so replaying an event is harmless. SHA-256 is the fingerprint used to pin versions.

terms.term: Memoization / case-based reasoning / KEDB / KCS / elastic-recheck
terms.definition: Reusing earlier answers; solving by retrieving similar past cases; known-error database; knowledge-centred service; OpenStack's tool matching failures to known-bug queries.
terms.origin: Computer science, AI (Aamodt and Plaza 1994), ITIL, OpenStack.

terms.definition: ReasoningBank stores distilled lessons from agent failures (cut SWE-bench steps 4-9 %); Gloaguen et al. found repository context files raise cost over 20 % without general success gains.
Reciprocal rank fusion of rankings; generated paraphrases added at write time; a vector extension for SQLite; a small local embedding model.
Facebook's learned method for choosing which tests to run.
Data leaving the machine to an outside service, here the model provider.
The single place where heavy Docker-based checks may run so they do not collide.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the ship plan.

terms.definition: Proposed separate memory of verified solutions that a cheap model fetches, adapts and reuses instead of calling a stronger model. Never built; modelled in the pathway map.
terms.origin: Coined by the owner; knowledge-store PR #183 and harness v2 library section.

terms.definition: The order a failed problem climbs: one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable; the solution is stored on the way back.
terms.origin: Coined by us (owner's design) in the library goal.

terms.definition: The library model's cost unit: one call by the cheap model (Sonnet) costs 1; other costs are multiples of it.
The owner's five expectations: E1 big token cut over time; E2 faster responses and builds; E3 Sonnet at low effort matching Opus; E4 reuse across projects; E5 accurate, efficient lookups.
A model of the library as a graph of states work passes through, with chances and costs on each branch. It measures the mechanism and is not a forecast.
terms.origin: Coined by us; built in docs/program/library-pathways/.

terms.definition: Strong model directly (top_first), cheap model with the ladder (cheap_ladder), and cheap model with the library; all run on the same pieces of work.
One point where a result is produced and checked, about ten cheap calls, either visible or latent. A wrong output that passes the gate is an escape.
A chart starting with 100 pieces of work the cheap model would get wrong alone, showing how many remain wrong after each step toward a right answer.
terms.origin: Coined in the pathway page build.

terms.term: Three conditions (comes back, reach, entry quality)
terms.definition: Comes back: much work repeats; reach: an entry gets to the cheap model; entry quality: the entry is right and used rightly. A fourth group is running cost.
Corners set each condition group at its poor or good end; all-good puts every library unknown at its good end; tie is how strongly a group's unknowns move together (0 independent, 1 shared).
Alone: what moving only one limitation's unknowns gives; last: what is lost if only that one stays unsolved; both are shares of the full fall.
Running the model thousands of times with unknown settings drawn from their ranges to get a spread and ranking; a second meaning is a trained set of decision trees predicting a route.
terms.origin: Ensemble modelling; proposed by the owner.

terms.definition: A view listing every route from start to outcome with its chance and cost.
terms.origin: Reliability engineering; proposed by the owner.

terms.definition: Ids of the 69 limitations found by walking real cases through the library design's ten steps, each with two weights (54 seen in real cases, 15 from thought experiments).
The ten steps: task arrives, trigger, query, match, delivery, use, check, failure and ladder, capture, afterlife. Ten case families group real cases; ids like f10-1b name family and case.
terms.origin: Coined in the library design walks.

terms.definition: A misleading stored entry that matches a problem's symptoms but has a different cause.
Mechanical checks from stored entries moved into the shared test run so every piece of work passes them with no lookup.

Long-run limits on what the library could hold for exact, similar or composite problems, from outside studies; the oracle-match trial gives Sonnet the best earlier solution on held-out past problems and scores by tests.
Placeholder removed.

terms.term: Spec for hosts: Railway, Supabase, R2
terms.definition: Railway is the app host (old hostnames answer an edge 404); Supabase is managed Postgres, currently paused or dead; Cloudflare R2 stores media and backups.
Postgres 16 in test containers, 17 to match production; pg_restore restores a dump; Appendix C is the design recipe for a throwaway Postgres 17 restore.

terms.term: Backend gate tools (Alembic, ruff, mypy, lint-imports, pytest, pip-audit)
terms.definition: Migrations, lint and format, type check, import-boundary check, tests, and an advisory dependency vulnerability scan.
Test runners for mobile and web code.
The automated checks run on the repository (GitHub Actions; pins Node 22).

terms.term: Docker / container / Docker Desktop / WSL2 / Compose project
terms.definition: Docker runs isolated environments; Docker Desktop runs Linux containers in WSL2, a Linux virtual machine on Windows that holds much of this PC's memory; a Compose project is containers started together.
A Docker option letting the gates container use the database container's network so the database is at localhost.
Memory an operating system keeps for recently read files; the Docker VM held gigabytes Windows could not use.
Windows log entry for a restart without clean shutdown (24 on this PC); a bugcheck is a crash with a stop code, and 23 of 24 had code 0.
A Windows call preventing sleep while a program runs; hybrid sleep saves memory to disk before sleeping; mains is wall power; BitLocker is Windows disk encryption.
The third-party real-time scanner on this PC that blocks some DLLs during unpacking.
A Windows feature letting an Android emulator run hardware-accelerated without /dev/kvm.
A software phone for tests; ff34 is the one virtual device (Android 14, 2 GB RAM) set up on this PC.
Two versions of the JavaScript runtime; the project targets 22 and the machine has 24.

terms.term: Device lab (L3) / lab accounts / edge 404 stand-in
terms.definition: A native emulator rig with scripted protocols to rehearse drain and the offline matrix before a real phone; lab accounts and key are test-only; stand-in modes mimic the dead host (edge404), 5xx or a hang.
terms.origin: Coined in SHIP-PLAN section 7.5 and L3a.

terms.term: Expo / EAS / APK / expo prebuild / Gradle / assembleRelease
terms.definition: Expo is the React Native toolkit; EAS its build service; an APK the Android install file; expo prebuild generates native folders (forbidden in the repo); Gradle with assembleRelease builds a release APK.

terms.term: adb / dumpsys / logcat / apksigner / aapt2 / JDK
terms.definition: Android tools: adb talks to a phone, dumpsys and logcat read state and logs, apksigner checks signing, aapt2 reads APK info, a JDK runs Gradle.
Open-source mobile UI test tool that drives app screens from scripted flows, proposed for on-device smoke tests.
Phone maker (Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo) whose battery policies can kill background apps.

terms.term: Outbox / queues / drain / fleet drain protocol (O-10) / release/drain / hold notice
terms.definition: The phone's offline queue of unsent writes (never deleted); drain empties it into the recovered backend by an ordered protocol (O-10) on branch release/drain, after a hold notice telling technicians not to reset the app.
terms.origin: FixFlow mobile design (CLAUDE.md); coined in the ship plan.

terms.term: Fleet APK v1 / v2 / deploy train / T_close
terms.definition: v1 is the first drain build with P2a and P2b-1 only; v2 is built after P4c; the deploy train is behaviour-changing PRs merged before cutover; T_close ends the cutover window.
terms.origin: Coined by us in the ship plan.

terms.definition: Urdu: informal operational ledger (the app) versus formal approved ledger that flows to Odoo.
terms.origin: Urdu bookkeeping terms used by the owner.

terms.definition: Odoo is accounting software receiving the approved ledger; JSON-2 is its newer API; External IDs act as the exactly-once key.
Recovery point objective (how much data may be lost) and recovery time objective (how long recovery may take).

terms.term: ASVS / MASVS / SRB / FBR / NOT VALID then VALIDATE
terms.definition: OWASP security checklists for web and mobile; Sindh Revenue Board and Federal Board of Revenue (Pakistan taxes); a Postgres pattern adding a constraint without scanning, then validating rows later.

terms.term: TanStack DB / Cloudflare R2 / cloudflared / Caddy / Dependabot / VPS / git-shell / MSIX
terms.definition: Outside tools named in skills and the store design: offline-sync library, object storage, tunnel, web server, dependency updater, rented server, restricted git login shell, Windows app packaging.
TID251 is a Ruff lint rule banning named APIs such as hmac.compare_digest; compare_secret is our safe secret-compare helper because the raw call raises on non-ASCII strings.
terms.origin: Ruff linter; our code and CLAUDE.md.

terms.definition: Deploying the backend from the repo root rebuilt the API as the web SPA and caused a production outage; only deploying from backend/ is safe.
An existing generic security-audit skill that appsec-review-asvs builds on.

notes: Merged duplicates across readers (e.g. Harness, Clinic testbed, Refuter, Compaction, Cache read, Worktree, Gate, Journal). Ambiguous names kept as separate entries where meanings differ: B01-B21 vs loops B1-B5; W0-W2 stages vs W1-W5 weaknesses; L1-L3 levers vs L1-L4 phases; H1-H18 vs H1-H5; Footprint (slice) vs footprint in the knowledge store. One entry near the end ('Reaffirm / owner-critique terms') is an empty placeholder and should be dropped by the consumer; its content is covered by the Trace/early cutoff and write gate entries. Source paths for several docs (HARNESS-IDEAS-HORTHY, HARNESS-IDEAS-BAML, SKILLS-PACKAGES) are given as the readers cited them, without a confirmed directory.
